jobs.occupation: The Danish School of Education (DPU) at the Faculty of Arts, Aarhus University, invites applications for a position as an associate professor in educational and developmental psychology, commencing on 1 March 2027.
jobs.description:
Associate Professor in Educational and Developmental Psychology  

This is a full-time position commencing on 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

The position is based at DPU, at either the Aarhus campus or the Emdrup campus in Copenhagen. The selected applicant will be expected to participate in day-to-day activities at the school, including teaching and supervision. Some travel should be expected between the school’s campuses in Aarhus and Copenhagen. 

The position  

The position involves research and university teaching in the fields of educational and developmental psychology. The selected applicant will help further develop the existing research and teaching environment within the Department of Educational Anthropology and Educational Psychology, with a particular focus on developmental psychology in early childhood. 

The position involves teaching at Master’s level and conducting research in the fields of educational and developmental psychology. The selected applicant will become part of a well-established academic environment within the Department 

The selected applicant should be able to document experience conducting empirical research, both independently and in collaboration with others, including studies within childhood developmental psychology, using qualitative, quantitative and/or mixed methods. 

Preference will be given to applicants who can document an interest in one or more of the following research areas: Transitions between institutions and families; family life, children’s psychological, emotional and relational development in and across different settings. 

Preference will be given to applicants able to teach and supervise in psychological and educational assessments and psychometrics. 

Research  

The selected applicant will be expected to: 

• develop new research projects relevant to the field of educational and developmental psychology 
• contribute to collaborative research initiatives at DPU, both nationally and internationally 
• pursue external research funding 
• contribute to theoretical, methodological and empirical developments in the fields of early childhood and/or childhood studies and/or family studies. 
• Applicants must outline their vision and plans for contributing to the suggested research fields. 
Teaching  

The selected applicant will teach and supervise students at all levels across relevant degree programmes at DPU, particularly the Master’s degree programme in educational psychology, including the specialisation in educational psychological counselling (PPR) and related electives, as well as in the field of early childhood. Teaching may also be expected on the professional Master’s degree programme in well-being. 

Talent development  

Associate professors at DPU/AU are expected to continuously develop their competences in supervising students at the Master’s and PhD levels, including the development and teaching of PhD courses focusing on theory, methodology and/or specific methods in collaboration with colleagues. Applicants are invited to describe their experiences of and plans or ideas for talent development. 

Knowledge exchange  

The selected applicant will be expected to engage in knowledge exchange as described in the strategy of the Faculty of Arts, for instance through collaboration on research with external partners, public dissemination activities, consultancy work or collaboration with relevant stakeholders. Applicants should document any prior experience of knowledge exchange activities and outline their plans for maximising the impact of their research within educational and developmental psychology and its implications for practice. 

Qualifications  

Applicants must hold a PhD degree or equivalent qualifications in a relevant field and be able to document: 

• a research profile within developmental psychology in the fields of daycare/reception class and/or family life, as well as children’s psychological and relational development in early childhood 
• an international publication profile, including experience of participation in international networks 
• experience applying for and obtaining external research funding 
• knowledge of and interest in psychodynamic–relational theories of personality, identity and selfhood from a developmental perspective, whether from a supportive and/or a critical position. 
• experience conducting empirical research, preferably using a range of methodologies relevant to the field of developmental psychology 
• knowledge of psychological tests and assessment tools relevant to early childhood and developmental psychology. 
Further information  
For further information about the position, please contact the head of the Department of Educational Anthropology and Educational Psychology, Charlotte Mathiassen, email: cham@edu.au.dk, tel.: +45 6186 3645. 

The application must be submitted in English. 

About the Danish School of Education  

The Danish School of Education (DPU) is one of the three schools at the Faculty of Arts, Aarhus University. 

Across its two locations at Campus Emdrup in Copenhagen and Nobel Park in Aarhus, DPU is home to approximately 200 academic and administrative staff, as well as approximately 80 PhD students. 

Our degree programmes  

The Danish School of Education currently offers a Bachelor’s degree programme in educational studies and ten Master’s degree programmes in a range of educational and pedagogical disciplines, as well as six professional Master’s degree programmes that can also be studied as single-subject courses. 

Approximately 2,000 students are enrolled in the school’s Bachelor’s and Master’s degree programmes, with approximately 250 students enrolled in professional Master’s degree programmes. 

Many of these programmes are offered at DPU’s locations in both Copenhagen and Aarhus, with students fairly evenly divided between the two campuses. 

Our research  

The Danish School of Education is Denmark's largest university environment for basic and applied research in pedagogy and education. 

The school is home to strong research environments within educational studies, educational theory and curriculum studies, general education, educational psychology, educational anthropology, educational sociology and educational philosophy, 

In addition, we conduct interdisciplinary research focused on specific educational fields of inquiry, particularly schools and early childhood education and care. 

DPU promotes public awareness of research in education and pedagogy through extensive dissemination activities with the aim of providing society with a rich and robust knowledge base. 

International applicants  

International applicants are encouraged to read about family and work-life balance as well as the attractive working conditions and other benefits of working at Aarhus University and in Denmark, including healthcare, paid holidays and, if relevant, maternity/paternity leave, childcare and schooling. Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including a relocation service and career counselling for expat partners. For information about taxation, see the taxation aspects of international researchers’ employment by AU. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here: http://international.au.dk/research/ 

An appointee who does not speak Danish will be required to acquire proficiency in Danish to handle tasks, including administrative and managerial responsibilities, and to participate fully in the activities of the Danish School of Education within approximately two years of commencing the appointment. These activities include, but are not limited to, teaching and examining students, reading work-related texts and participating in meetings and collegial gatherings in Danish. 

Formalities
• Faculty of Arts refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities (the Appointment Order).
• Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.
• Further information on the application and supplementary materials may be found in Application Guidelines.
• The application must outline the applicant's motivation for applying for the position, attaching a curriculum vitae, a teaching portfolio, a complete list of published works, a research plan, copies of degree certificates and no more than five examples of academic production (mandatory).
Please upload this material electronically along with your application.

If nothing else is noted, applications must be submitted in English. Application deadline is at 11.59 pm Danish time (same as Central European Time) on the deadline day.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Shortlists may be prepared with the candidates that have been selected for a detailed academic assessment. A committee set up by the head of school is responsible for selecting the most qualified candidates. See this link for further information about shortlisting at the Faculty of Arts: shortlisting

Terms of employment
• Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations.
• Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as (xxx) at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).
The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

About ArtsThe Faculty of Arts is one of Northern Europe’s most significant faculties for research and higher education in the humanities, theology and education. Within this broad academic scope, the faculty comprises approximately 700 researchers, 200 PhD students, 9,000 Bachelor’s and Master’s degree students, and 1,500 further and continuing education students. We believe that the best ideas arise when different perspectives meet – and that research, teaching and innovation are best developed in dialogue with the surrounding society.

You can find more information here: Faculty of Arts | Aarhus University

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

The Impact You'll Make

At Danfoss, great decisions start with great data. As our new Student Worker in Production Engineering, you will play a hands-on role in building the documentation and data foundation that drives smarter, faster decisions across our production environment. Your working hours will be split equally between our sites in Christiansfeld and Marsvej (Kolding), so you will be working on the production floor at both locations.

You will help uncover where processes can be stabilized, improved, and made more transparent. Whether it is through a well-structured analysis or a small improvement initiative you take ownership of, the work you do here creates real operational value, and you will see the results directly.

This is a role for someone who is curious, self-driven, and ready to work where engineering meets data. You will move between your desk and the production floor across both sites, collaborating with operators, engineers, and supervisors who are genuinely invested in making things better.

What You’ll Be Doing

• 
Strengthen production documentation by creating, maintaining, and improving process records that give the whole team a clearer picture of how work gets done.

• 
Turn data into decisions by analysing production output and preparing insights that support continuous improvement across the organization.

• 
Dig into production challenges alongside engineers and operators to identify root causes and flag where process stabilization is needed.

• 
Drive small improvement initiatives end-to-end, from identifying the opportunity based on data to proposing and testing your own solutions.

• 
Support the production engineering team with a varied mix of tasks, giving you broad exposure to engineering operations in a real industrial environment.

What We're Looking For

• 
Strong Excel skills and a solid foundation for working with and interpreting data.

• 
A curious, problem-solving mindset. You ask questions, explore issues, and aren't afraid to form your own view.

• 
The ability to work autonomously and take ownership, managing your time independently while knowing when to collaborate.

• 
Good written and spoken English. Danish is a plus in our day-to-day team environment.

• 
Currently enrolled in a relevant engineering, data, or technical degree programme.

What You'll Get from Us

• 
We promote from within and support your learning with mentoring, training, and access to global opportunities.

• 
You’ll have flexibility, autonomy, and support to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Your well-being matters to us.

• 
We strive to create an inclusive work environment where people of all backgrounds are respected and valued for who they are.

• 
You’ll receive benefits like annual bonus, paid vacation, pension plans, personal insurance, and more. These vary by country and contract, but they’re worth asking about—we think they’re great.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

Our Commitment to Transparency

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Any benefits listed do not promise or guarantee any particular benefit or specific action. They may depend on country or contract specifics and are subject to change at any time without prior notice.

Want to know more? Please visit our FAQ Page.

We also provide solutions for data centers, renewable energy, energy storage, heat recovery, as well as contribute to district energy solutions for cities.

jobs.occupation: Head of Center of Excellence for Project Management
jobs.description:
At Bavarian Nordic, we are committed to saving and improving lives by unlocking the power of the immune system. Our commercial portfolio includes market-leading vaccines against smallpox/mpox, rabies, tick-borne encephalitis, typhoid fever, and cholera. We excel in R&D innovation, manufacturing, and commercialization, working every day to protect people’s health and quality of life and protect our tomorrow.

We are looking for an experienced leader for the Head of Center of Excellence (project management) role in our Strategy Execution department who combines strategic thinking, strong change management capabilities, and a genuine passion for building organizational capability. In this role, you will not only define how projects are governed and delivered but also drive the adoption of new ways of working across a global organization.

**About The Role

**This is a broad and hands-on role spanning project leadership and organizational capability building within project excellence. A key aspect of the role is driving organizational change by ensuring that project management frameworks, tools, and processes are successfully adopted, understood, and embedded across the business. In this dual role, you will balance being Head of Center of Excellence while managing high-impact cross-functional projects yourself. Just as importantly, you will turn standards into practice by designing and delivering training, facilitating sessions, coaching colleagues, and creating engagement across the organization.

You will work across R&D, manufacturing, supply chain, commercial, and corporate functions. The portfolio may include merger and acquisition activities, development projects, vaccine launches, technology implementations, and other enterprise-wide transformation initiatives. Success requires someone who enjoys moving between strategic planning, practical implementation, and visible facilitation in front of an audience.

The position is based in Hellerup, Denmark. You will join a team of +20 Project Managers, Program Leads, and Student Assistants and report to the VP of Strategy Execution Office.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Own and continuously strengthen project management standards, governance, tools, templates, and ways of working across the organization

• Lead complex, cross-functional strategic projects, including initiatives connected to M&A, product development, vaccine launches, and enterprise transformation

• Drive adoption of project management methodologies and support organizational change through stakeholder engagement, communication, training, and coaching

• Develop project management capability through structured training, facilitation, coaching, and hands-on knowledge sharing across different functions and seniority levels

• Serve as a visible ambassador for project excellence, translating methodology into clear, practical, and engaging learning experiences

• Partner with senior stakeholders to create alignment, transparency, sound decision-making, and clear ownership throughout the project lifecycle

• Drive disciplined planning, risk management, resource coordination, and execution, supported by strong use of project and portfolio management tools

**What You Bring

**You bring extensive experience leading complex projects within pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, vaccines, or another highly regulated healthcare environment. You also bring change management expertise combined with hands-on delivery experience. Besides this, we are looking for someone with the following background;

• A genuine interest in the full scope of project management excellence, from strategic framework design and governance to practical implementation and organizational training

• Strong presentation and facilitation skills, with the confidence and energy to stand in front of an audience, engage participants, and make complex methods practical and relevant

• Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, create buy-in, and lead through complex global and cross-functional environments

• Strong knowledge of PMI-based project management practices. PMI/PMP certification is an advantage - other relevant certifications are also valued

• Experience with merger and acquisition projects

• A relevant master’s degree within life sciences, engineering, supply chain, business, or a related field

• Advanced expertise in Smartsheet combined with experience with Microsoft Project is an advantage

**Why join us?

**This role gives you the opportunity to influence both how strategic projects are delivered and how project management capability is built across Bavarian Nordic. You will combine high-impact project leadership with the chance to shape standards, develop colleagues, and create a lasting project excellence culture in a purpose-driven global vaccine organization.

If you are motivated by strategy and execution, enjoy building practical solutions, and feel energized by training and engaging others, we would love to hear from you.

**Caught your interest?

**Apply now and join Bavarian Nordic in our mission to improve health outcomes and foster sustainable growth.

We do not offer any relocation packages for this role. Please note that employment is contingent on residing and working in Denmark.

We kindly request that headhunters or recruitment agencies refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

_Bavarian Nordic is a global vaccine company with a mission to improve health and save lives through innovative vaccines. We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. We are headquartered in Denmark and have manufacturing, research, and sales offices across Europe and North America.

__Bavarian Nordic is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applications will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

_For more information, visit www.bavarian-nordic.com

Would you like to manage renewable energy portfolios across European power markets – and use your quantitative skills to make better commercial decisions?

Join our Physical Asset Management team and take responsibility for your own areas of the portfolio. You will work hands-on with market analysis, quantitative models, pricing and PnL while building the market knowledge needed to spot where we can do things better.

The team

You will join Physical Asset Management at Norlys Energy Trading in Aalborg. We manage renewable energy portfolios across European power markets, combining portfolio management with market analysis and quantitative methods. The work involves close interaction with colleagues across trading, origination and asset management.

The role

As a Quant Researcher, you will operate and develop parts of our renewable portfolio across Europe. Over time, you will become the go-to person for your areas of responsibility: understanding what moves the market, how it affects the portfolio and where there is room to improve performance.

The role has a strong quantitative element. You will build models to understand portfolio effects, develop PnL dashboards and work on pricing methodologies and trading automation. You will also investigate new markets and products and help turn promising ideas into new business.

Key responsibilities

The role combines running the portfolio today with improving how we work tomorrow. You will work independently on some areas and together with colleagues and stakeholders in others.

• Maintain and operate our renewable portfolios across the EU.

• Run your own areas of responsibility with a focus on profitable performance.

• Follow your markets closely and build specialist knowledge within your areas.

• Build and maintain quantitative models to analyse and optimise portfolio effects.

• Develop pricing methodologies and identify ways to improve portfolio performance.

• Build and maintain dashboards that show PnL for your portfolios.

• Help automate trading tools and processes.

• Investigate new markets and products that could create new business opportunities. Work closely with key stakeholders and take part in relevant conferences and excursions.

The people who thrive in this kind of role are the ones who stay curious when the answer isn’t obvious. You’ll have room to dig into problems, form your own view and act on what you learn. And when the market changes, you need to be comfortable changing your mind with it.

Peter Lumbye Thomsen

Head of Intraday Analytics

What we are looking for

You are comfortable working with numbers, code and complex market information, but analysis is not an end in itself for you. You want to use it to make decisions, improve the way we work and move things forward when the market changes.

We expect you to have:

• An advanced degree in a quantitative field such as physics, economics, data science or mathematics.

• Strong programming skills in Python, R or a similar language.

• Experience with data analysis and statistical modelling.

• Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

• A can-do attitude and a sense of urgency when something needs to move.

• An understanding of why agility and speed-to-market matter in a changing market.

• The ability to work well with different stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.

• Experience within power trading or finance is an advantage, but not a requirement.

What we offer

• The role gives you room to build specialist knowledge while working hands-on with renewable portfolios across European power markets.

• Your own areas of responsibility within renewable portfolio management.

• The chance to build specialist knowledge of European power markets.

• A role that combines quantitative work with commercial decision-making.

• Exposure to new markets, products and business opportunities.

• Close collaboration with colleagues and stakeholders across the business.

• Participation in relevant conferences and excursions.

Interested?

If the combination of power markets, quantitative analysis and portfolio responsibility sounds like a good match for you, we would like to hear from you.

Want to know more?

Feel free to reach out if you have any questions about this opportunity

Peter Lumbye Thomsen

Head of Intraday Analytics

plt@norlysenergytrading.com

Would you like to take the lead in turning business opportunities into digital solutions that create measurable commercial impact?

As Digital Business Transformation Lead, you will help execute Hartmann’s European commercial strategy by identifying, shaping and delivering digital initiatives that improve customer experience and commercial efficiency. Reporting to the Commercial Excellence Director, Europe, you will work across markets and functions to turn business needs into practical solutions with measurable impact.

You will own the business side of agreed initiatives from discovery and concept development through implementation, adoption and benefits realisation. Group IT and technology partners will own architecture, cybersecurity and technical solution design.

Key responsibilities

• Identify and evaluate digital opportunities with customers and stakeholders across Hartmann’s European commercial organisation.

• Translate needs into customer journeys, future-state processes, concepts, prototypes and business requirements.

• Build business cases and support prioritisation of the European commercial digital portfolio.

• Lead the business side of agreed initiatives from discovery through implementation and adoption.

• Establish milestones, governance, risks, responsibilities and benefits tracking.

• Partner with Group IT and external providers while keeping customer needs and business outcomes central.

• Drive adoption through stakeholder engagement, communication, training and performance measurement.

Your experience and approach

You bring approximately 5–8 years of relevant experience in digital business transformation, product ownership, consulting or complex cross-functional delivery.

We expect you to have:

• Strong commercial and process understanding

• Experience taking unclear opportunities from discovery to implementation and adoption

• Ability to create structure, influence senior stakeholders and secure cross-functional commitment

• Working knowledge of digital platforms, data, automation and AI

• Strong English and sufficient Danish for informal workplace communication

Experience from manufacturing or an international B2B environment is valuable, but your ability to understand customers and turn business needs into practical improvements matters most.

You are curious, pragmatic and proactive. You create direction in ambiguous situations, test ideas quickly and remain hands-on until solutions are adopted and create value.

Hartmann offers

You will join an international company with more than 100 years of history and a strong position in the global food packaging industry.

The role offers:

• Ownership of visible European digital initiatives.

• Direct collaboration with customers, commercial leadership and Group IT.

• Freedom to test practical applications of digital solutions, automation and AI.

• An international role combining strategy, discovery and hands-on execution.

You will be responsible for translating Hartmann Europe’s commercial digital priorities into adopted solutions and measurable business improvements—not for defining enterprise technology strategy or owning technical architecture.

Location

The position is based at Hartmann’s headquarters in Lyngby, Denmark, with a flexible hybrid working arrangement. Expect approximately 10–20 travel days per year, primarily within Europe.

Contact and application

Hartmann is assisted in this recruitment process by European Search Company.

For more information, please contact Christoffer Bjørk Petersen on +45 2080 1638 or Brian Ranvits on +45 2048 0548.

Please submit your application using the apply button below. We review applications as they arrive and encourage you to apply at your earliest convenience.

About Hartmann Packaging

Founded in 1917, Hartmann is headquartered in Lyngby, Denmark. Hartmann is the world’s leading specialist in moulded fibre egg packaging and a trusted partner in the global food supply chain.

With more than 100 years of experience, we combine deep technology and manufacturing expertise with a strong global presence to design, produce, and deliver innovative moulded fibre products. In doing so, we provide sustainable packaging that helps feed the world – one carton at a time.

Hartmann employs approximately 2,800 employees across Europe, North America, South America, and APAC. Hartmann is part of the THORNICO Group

jobs.occupation: Take ownership of AML, KYC, risk and compliance in Secure Payment (part of AutoProff)
jobs.description:
Secure Payment is the payment entity within AutoProff, handling payments related to our car auctions across the business. We’re looking for a AML, KYC, Risk & Compliance Specialist to take ownership of our compliance framework and help ensure that Secure Payment remains well governed, structured and compliant as we continue to develop the business.

This is a broad and hands-on role where you’ll work closely with management, the Board of Directors and colleagues across Tech, Support and Finance.

At AutoProff, we’re changing the way used vehicles are traded across Europe. Every day, thousands of vehicles are bought and sold through our platform, connecting professional car dealers across markets.

About the role

As our new AML, KYC, Risk & Compliance Specialist, you’ll join Secure Payment and be based at our headquarters in Vejle, Denmark.

You’ll take responsibility for AML, KYC, risk and compliance activities and help ensure that policies, processes, controls and documentation are kept up to date and work effectively in practice.

The role has a broad stakeholder landscape and combines structured compliance work with reporting, administration and practical follow-up. You’ll work closely with the Board of Directors, management, customers and colleagues across AutoProff, including Tech, Support and Finance.

Secure Payment is also developing a new reporting methodology, and you’ll have the opportunity to help shape how we structure management information, controls and reporting going forward.

What you’ll be doing

Your responsibilities will include:

• Own and further develop Secure Payment’s AML, KYC, risk and compliance activities

• Maintain and improve relevant policies, procedures, controls and documentation

• Coordinate and follow up on KYC reviews, customer due diligence, monitoring and relevant AML cases

• Identify, assess and follow up on compliance and operational risks

• Prepare clear and structured reporting for management and the Board of Directors

• Help develop Secure Payment’s reporting methodology and management information

• Follow up on findings, incidents, regulatory requirements and agreed actions

• Work closely with colleagues across Tech, Support, Finance and the wider AutoProff organisation

• Explore how AI and digital tools can support reporting, documentation and compliance processes

• Maintain constructive dialogue with relevant internal and external stakeholders

What we’re looking for

We imagine you have experience with AML and KYC, or a solid understanding of the underlying principles combined with a strong interest in developing your regulatory and legal knowledge further.

More specifically, we’re looking for someone with:

• Experience with AML, KYC or related compliance activities

• A structured and administrative approach to work

• Strong attention to detail and a focus on high-quality documentation and reporting

• The ability to maintain an overview and prioritise when several tasks are moving at the same time

• An interest in compliance, risk and regulatory topics

• Good understanding of IT systems and digital tools

• Strong written and verbal communication skills in Danish and English

• Confidence working independently and taking ownership of your area

Beyond your experience, we’re looking for someone who is structured, curious and hands-on, and who enjoys creating order, following up and making sure things are done properly.

Nice to have

It’s a plus, but not a requirement, if you have experience with:

• Banking, payment institutions, financial services or another regulated environment

• Risk and compliance in a regulated business

• Reporting to senior management or a Board of Directors

• A banking or financial-services background

• Using AI or digital tools to improve reporting, documentation or compliance processes

Why join AutoProff?

At AutoProff, you’ll become part of an international company that is changing the way used cars are traded across Europe.

You’ll work with colleagues across countries and functions in an environment where there is room to take ownership, share ideas and influence how we do things. We move quickly, work closely together and value people who are comfortable taking responsibility while also asking for input when needed.

As part of AutoScout24 Group, we combine the pace and hands-on environment of AutoProff with the opportunities and international reach of one of Europe’s leading automotive marketplaces.

In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to shape a developing compliance function, work closely with senior stakeholders and influence how Secure Payment structures its AML, KYC, risk and reporting processes going forward.

Ready to join us?

If this sounds like an opportunity you’d like to explore, we’d like to hear from you.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and may close the position once we have found the right candidate.

About AutoProff

AutoProff was founded in Denmark in 2013 with one goal: to make B2B used-car trading simpler and more efficient through digital solutions.

Today, AutoProff provides online B2B used-car trading solutions for professional car dealers across Europe, with more than 150,000 vehicles traded through our platforms annually.

In August 2022, AutoScout24, one of Europe’s leading online automotive marketplaces, acquired a majority stake in AutoProff. Together, we are working towards creating a fully integrated C2B-B2B-B2C solution for used cars across Europe.

Our ambition is simple: to be the home of B2B car trading for European car dealers.

Shape the future of trusted digital signing

Join Cryptomathic's Signer team and help build secure software that enables trusted digital signatures and seals for governments, financial institutions, and trust service providers worldwide.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you'll work on a complex, business-critical platform where security, reliability, and compliance are essential. You'll be part of a small, experienced team with significant influence over technical decisions while remaining hands-on and close to the code.

About Signer

Signer is Cryptomathic's electronic signing platform, enabling trust service providers, governments, and financial institutions to deliver legally binding electronic signatures and seals. Built on industry standards and aligned with eIDAS, Signer helps customers implement trusted digital signing solutions at scale while meeting demanding security and compliance requirements.

What you'll do

About Memtrace

AI coding agents are fast, but they forget. They lose context between sessions, repeat mistakes, and don't understand the codebase around them. Memtrace builds the memory layer that fixes this: a deterministic knowledge graph of your code, built with AST parsing rather than guesswork, that any coding agent can use. Our products include MemDB, MemFleet, Cortex, and a code review engine. We are backed by Antler and Innovation Fund Denmark, and we work with Google, AWS, and Microsoft for Startups.

You will own revenue end to end: strategy, pipeline, pricing, partnerships, and the first commercial team. We have developer interest and active pilots with enterprise customers. Your job is to turn that into repeatable, paying adoption. At this stage you will do the selling yourself while building the playbook that others will follow.

jobs.occupation: Tracking Microbes Across Borders using Genomics to Uncover Biomass-to-Biogas Transmission Pathways
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for Husdyr- og Veter
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Animal and Veterinary Sciences programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Tracking Microbes Across Borders using Genomics to Uncover Biomass-to-Biogas Transmission Pathways

Research area and project description
Biogas production supports the transition to renewable energy and a circular bioeconomy. However, the increasing use of imported animal-derived biomass creates connected biosecurity interfaces between European suppliers, international transport, Danish reception points, biogas plants and nearby livestock production. This PhD project will determine whether these pathways are microbiologically plausible and identify where hygienisation and other biosecurity barriers interrupt them.

Using a risk-informed longitudinal design, the candidate will sample linked compartments including incoming biomass vehicles, reception and unloading areas, local vehicles and machinery, plant environments, biomass before and after hygienisation, and selected onward-facing interfaces. The project will combine targeted PCR/RT-qPCR surveillance for epidemiologically relevant transboundary animal-disease agents and other animal pathogens with long-read shotgun metagenomics, culture and viability approaches, and sequencing of selected isolates. Comparative genomic analyses will assess microbial connectivity between compartments while distinguishing co-detection from evidence consistent with persistence or transfer. Findings will be integrated with biomass origin and type, transport history, season and plant/process conditions.

Controlled experiments will quantify persistence, transfer and inactivation under representative transport, storage, cleaning/disinfection and processing conditions. Where work with high-consequence agents is not feasible, appropriate surrogates, indicators or non-infectious materials will be used. The project will deliver evidence on microbial hazards, resistomes, mobile genetic elements, critical control points and effective biosecurity barriers in the Danish biogas sector.

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants to the PhD position must hold a relevant master’s degree, or an equivalent qualification, in Genomics, veterinary science, microbiology, molecular biology, bioinformatics, or a closely related discipline.

Relevant experience in molecular microbiology, microbial genomics/metagenomics, culture-based microbiology, bioinformatics or quantitative data analysis is an advantage; applicants are not expected to be experts in all areas.

The successful candidate should be motivated to combine field sampling, laboratory experiments and computational analysis; work carefully under appropriate biosafety and quality procedures; collaborate across institutions and with external stakeholders; and communicate effectively in written and spoken English. A driving license and willingness to travel to Danish biogas plants are advantages.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Aarhus University, Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences, Blichers Allé 20, 8830 Tjele, Denmark.

Contacts
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
 
• Yaovi Mahuton Gildas Hounmanou, gil@anivet.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Anders Dalsgaard, adal@sund.ku.dk (co-supervisor)
• Karl Pedersen, karl.pedersen@anivet.au.dk (co-supervisor)
For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk
How to apply
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 01 November 2026 at 23:59 CET.
Preferred starting date is 01 January 2027.

For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Please note:
• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.
• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.
Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which everyone has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via the online recruitment system, which can be accessed under ‘How to apply’.
